topic: How do GEO and LEO constellations trade off coverage area versus latency in 5G NTN architectures?
consensus_response: The trade-off between GEO and LEO constellations in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) architectures lies in their distinct characteristics. GEO satellites offer global coverage but introduce significant delays (up to 238 ms) due to the longer distance between the satellite and user equipment (UE). In contrast, LEO constellations provide reduced propagation delays but require more satellites for global coverage, increasing interference and complexity. A good Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP) is crucial for precise timing advance estimation in LEO constellations, improving signal propagation and reducing latency. Well-designed satellite constellation geometry minimizes interference between adjacent satellite beams, ensuring reliable communication.
reference_context: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) mega constellations are gaining attention due to their ability to provide global coverage and reduced propagation delays compared to Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites.
